@ctruhtech/verse-sdk — JavaScript / TypeScript client#

The typed, dependency-free client for everything in the API reference: upload a model (one-shot or resumable, with progress and cancel), follow the compile with stage callbacks, own, share, version, review and measure the scene, and mount the viewer on your page. Works in Node 18+ and every modern browser; ESM and CommonJS; full TypeScript typings; nothing but fetch.

Code
sdk/                      the package (source, tests, examples)
  src/index.ts            one file — the whole client
  src/embed-types.d.ts    copied from web/playground/verse-embed.d.ts at build
  dist/esm, dist/cjs      `npm run build` (plain tsc, no bundler)
  examples/               Node CLI, HTML embed page, GitHub Actions
web/playground/sdk/       the served copy: /sdk/verse-sdk.js (+ .d.ts)

Install#

From npm (when published) or straight from the repo:

Code
npm install @ctruhtech/verse-sdk          # ESM + CJS + types
# or, in this repository:
cd sdk && npm install && npm run build
Code
import { VerseClient } from "@ctruhtech/verse-sdk";              // ESM / TypeScript
// CommonJS: const { VerseClient } = require("@ctruhtech/verse-sdk");

Or with no package manager at all — the Verse origin serves the ESM build exactly like embed.js, with the same Cache-Control: no-cache + ETag headers (the browser revalidates; a deploy is picked up on the next load):

Code
<script type="module">
  import { VerseClient } from "/sdk/verse-sdk.js";   // a page on the Verse origin
</script>

Typings for that copy: https://HOST/sdk/verse-sdk.d.ts (+ embed-types.d.ts).

Where the browser build runs. Since 4.0 /sdk/verse-sdk.js (like embed.js and /sdk/verse-viewer.js) is served with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin, so a page on another origin can import it. The API itself sends no CORS headers on /v1/* — a server policy the SDK does not change (see Warts) — so from a third-party page embedViewer() works everywhere (the engine runs in an iframe from the Verse origin), while API calls go through your own backend with the package (Node 18+), or from pages you host on the Verse origin itself.

Auth#

Code
const verse = new VerseClient({
  baseUrl: "https://verse.ctruh.com", // or your own origin
  token: process.env.VERSE_TOKEN,   // account token (64 hex) → Authorization: Bearer — owns what you upload
  apiKey: process.env.VERSE_API_KEY, // vk_… → X-API-Key — only on keyed-mode servers
  share: null,                       // a share token for ONE private scene → X-Verse-Share
});

All three are optional (Authentication). Get an account token once with createAccount() (it is shown once — store it like an API key). Other options: source (tool attribution, default verse-sdk/<version>), retries (transient retries, default 1), telemetry (see Telemetry opt-out), pollIntervalMs (default 3000), fetch (custom implementation).

Three calls: file in, link out#

Code
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { VerseClient } from "@ctruhtech/verse-sdk";

const verse = new VerseClient({ baseUrl: "https://HOST", token: process.env.VERSE_TOKEN });
const scene = await verse.publish(readFileSync("flat.glb"), {
  name: "flat",
  onProgress: (p) => p.fraction !== undefined && console.log(`upload ${(p.fraction * 100) | 0}%`),
  onStage: (stage, rec) => console.log(stage, rec.etaText ?? ""),
});
console.log(scene.url);                  // https://HOST/?vpk=ingest/flat-….vpk
console.log(verse.shareLink(scene));     // https://HOST/view?vpk=ingest/flat-….vpk

publish() is upload() + waitForJob(); use them separately to store the job id across process restarts.

Errors#

Every failure is a VerseError with the API's error contract decoded:

FieldMeaning
messagethe server's error sentence, verbatim — safe to show
statusHTTP status; 0 for a network error, cancel or timeout
codethe friendly-error code when the server gave one (no_meshes, file_too_large, …), else auth_required / not_found / rate_limited / server_busy / storage_full / network / edge / cancelled / timeout / unknown_job / job_failed
fromApptrue = the Verse server spoke (X-Verse-Error: 1): authoritative, do not blind-retry. false = the network edge or the network itself
retryableis trying again worthwhile?
errorInfo{ code, title, message, fix, retryable } from an ingest failure
bodythe parsed JSON body (e.g. received on a 409)

Transient failures (fromApp: false) are retried once by every call (retries option); app errors never are.

Code
import { VerseError } from "@ctruhtech/verse-sdk";
try {
  await verse.publish(bytes);
} catch (e) {
  if (e instanceof VerseError && e.code === "no_meshes") console.log(e.errorInfo.fix);
  else throw e;
}

Reference#

Every method, the route it calls (API reference), and a runnable example. verse is a VerseClient.

Ingest#

limits() — GET /v1/limits#

What to know before choosing a file: enforced limits, recommendations, the texture budget, timing, the live queue.

Code
const { limits, recommended } = await verse.limits();
if (file.size > limits.maxUploadBytes) throw new Error("too big");

upload(file, options?) — POST /v1/ingest, or the resumable trio#

Upload bytes (Blob/File, Buffer, Uint8Array, ArrayBuffer); resolves { job } once the server accepted them. Options:

OptionMeaning
nameslug prefix for the scene id (X-Verse-Name)
kind: "splat" | "cloud" | "ifc" | "usd" | "fbx" | "obj"a .splat/.ply capture, a point cloud (.ply/.las/.laz/.e57 → streamed .vpc), an IFC building model or a single-file USD scene (both converted on the server; the record then carries propsUrl and convert), or (3.0) an FBX / OBJ model, alone or zipped with its textures (converted on the server, then published like a GLB; the record carries convert) (X-Verse-Kind; the bytes are sniffed anyway)
units: "m" | "cm" | "mm" | "in" | "ft"(3.0) OBJ only — the unit the file was authored in (X-Verse-Units); by default a model wider than 1,000 units is read as centimetres. FBX declares its own
resumable"auto" (default: resumable at ≥ 100 MB, like the exporters), true, false
resumableFromBytes, partBytesthe auto threshold (100 MB) and part size (8 MB)
prepared: truethe file went through verse-prepare; lifts the resumable cap to 20 GB (checked at commit)
bake: true | "preview" | "final"(2.7) Bake for me: lightmap a live-lit GLB on the server before compiling (X-Verse-Bake; true = "preview"). The job record's bake carries the report, or bake.skipped when the scene was compiled live-lit instead
path: "fidelity" | "streamed"(2.8) Fidelity mode: publish the file itself as ingest/<id>.fidelity.glb (X-Verse-Path) — the record then carries path, glbUrl, classification, digest/signature. Omitted = streamed, with the classifier's verdict in classification
look: "studio:warm,bg:ffffff"(2.8) with path: "fidelity": the studio preset (neutral / warm / dark) and backdrop the share link opens with (X-Verse-Look)
onProgress(p){ sent, total, fraction, part?, resumedFrom? } — per part when resumable; 0 and 1 for a one-shot upload in Node, live in browsers (XHR)
signalan AbortSignal — cancel; rejects with code: "cancelled"
Code
const ctl = new AbortController();
cancelButton.onclick = () => ctl.abort();
const { job } = await verse.upload(fileInput.files[0], {
  name: "showroom",
  onProgress: (p) => (bar.value = p.fraction),
  signal: ctl.signal,
});

uploadResumable(file, options?) — POST /v1/ingest/begin · PUT /v1/ingest/part/<uploadId> · GET /v1/ingest/part/<uploadId> · POST /v1/ingest/commit/<uploadId>#

The resumable flow explicitly: strictly ordered parts; a dropped connection waits, reads the server's received and carries on; an out-of-order 409 moves the cursor to the server's offset, a 409 at the client's own offset ("another part is already uploading") backs off and retries; up to 8 misses in a row (~1 min) before it gives up, and a resync that itself fails at the network counts as one more miss. Network errors name the socket error Node's fetch hides in cause (network error: fetch failed (ECONNRESET: …)). commit answers the same 202 { job } as a one-shot upload. Resolves { job, uploadId }.

Code
const { job, uploadId } = await verse.uploadResumable(bigBuffer, { name: "scan", partBytes: 16 * 1024 * 1024,
  onProgress: (p) => console.log(`part ${p.part ?? "-"} ${(p.fraction * 100).toFixed(0)}%`) });

uploadFromUrl(url, options?) — POST /v1/ingest/url · publishFromUrl(url, options?)#

4.0: the server fetches a public http(s) URL (Dropbox dl=1, a presigned S3 link, a CMS media URL) and compiles it like an upload — the file never passes through your process. uploadFromUrl resolves { job, sizeBytes, source }; publishFromUrl waits for the compile and resolves the finished record. Options: name, kind, bake, path, look, signal (+ the wait options). Private / local addresses fail with code url_blocked; a link that does not hand over a file with url_fetch_failed.

Code
const rec = await verse.publishFromUrl("https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fi/…/villa.glb?dl=1", { name: "villa" });
console.log(rec.url);

job(jobId) — GET /v1/ingest/<job>#

One poll. The record's shape is documented at GET /v1/ingest/<job>; unknown_job after the two-hour record retention.

Code
const rec = await verse.job(job);
console.log(rec.status, rec.stage, rec.etaText);

waitForJob(jobId, options?)#

Poll until the job leaves compiling. Resolves the done record; rejects with a VerseError carrying the taxonomy code when it ends in error. Options: onStage(stage, record) (fires on every stage/status change), onProgress(record) (every poll), intervalMs, timeoutMs (default 45 min), missTolerance (default 8 missed polls — rides out a server restart), signal.

Code
const done = await verse.waitForJob(job, { onStage: (s) => console.log("→", s) });
// → preparing → queued → textures → geometry → packing → signing → verifying → done

publish(file, options?)#

upload() then waitForJob() with one options object; resolves the done record plus job. Byte progress is onUploadProgress; onProgress and onStage are the job poll's — before 4.0 onProgress received both shapes.

attachContact(jobId, contact) — POST /v1/ingest/<job>/contact#

"Email me when it's live." { name, email, phone, consent: true } → { ok, emailed, notify }.

Code
await verse.attachContact(job, { name: "Asha Rao", email: "asha@example.com", phone: "+91 98765 43210", consent: true });

shareLink(sceneOrRecord, options?)#

The viewer link for a scene id, a finished job record or a scene summary: https://HOST/view?vpk=ingest/<id>.vpk (a classic-fallback record keeps its own ?model= link). Knobs: share (a share token → ?share=, the private-scene gate that also unlocks GET /ingest/<id>.vpk?share=<shareToken>), variant (open on a material variant), view: "overview".

Code
verse.shareLink(done, { variant: "Oak", share: token.shareToken });

Accounts#

createAccount(name) — POST /v1/account#

Token-only accounts; the token is returned once (3 per day per IP). Does not set verse.token — you decide where it is stored.

Code
const { accountId, token } = await verse.createAccount("Acme Realty");

account() — GET /v1/account · accountStats() — GET /v1/account/stats#

Code
const me = await verse.account();                // { accountId, name, createdAt }
const { opens, last7d } = await verse.accountStats();

accountAnalytics({ days? }) — GET /v1/account/analytics · accountAnalyticsCsv({ days? }) — GET /v1/account/analytics.csv#

4.0: every owned scene added up over the last 7, 30 (default) or 90 days, plus a row per scene; the CSV variant returns the text of the attachment.

Code
const a = await verse.accountAnalytics({ days: 30 });   // { views, uniqueViewers, scenes: [{ id, views, … }] }

login(token?) — POST /v1/account/login · logout() — POST /v1/account/logout#

Browser sign-in for /studio (sets / clears the verse_session cookie). API clients just pass token to the constructor.

Code
await verse.login(token);

webhooks.list() — GET /v1/account/webhooks · webhooks.create({ url, events?, secret? }) — POST /v1/account/webhooks · webhooks.delete(id) — DELETE /v1/account/webhooks/<id> · webhooks.deliveries(id) — GET /v1/account/webhooks/<id>/deliveries#

Webhooks (2.7): signed, retried receivers for scene.ready, scene.failed, comment.added, version.promoted and config.changed (docs/api.md § Webhooks). The secret is on the create response once; list() only ever shows a hint.

Code
const hook = await verse.webhooks.create({ url: "https://example.com/verse-hook", events: ["scene.ready"] });
saveSomewhereSafe(hook.secret);
const { deliveries } = await verse.webhooks.deliveries(hook.id); // last 50, newest first
await verse.webhooks.delete(hook.id);

webhooks.test(id) — POST /v1/account/webhooks/<id>/test#

One signed ping delivery now, no retries → { id, delivery, ok, status, ms, error? }.

Code
const r = await verse.webhooks.test(hook.id);
if (!r.ok) console.warn(`receiver answered ${r.status || r.error}`);

verifyWebhook({ secret, body, signature, timestamp, toleranceSec? })#

For your receiver: recomputes X-Verse-Signature over the raw body in constant time and rejects timestamps more than toleranceSec (default 300) off. WebCrypto — Node 18+, Workers, Deno, Bun.

Code
import { verifyWebhook } from "@ctruhtech/verse-sdk";
const ok = await verifyWebhook({ secret, body: rawBody, signature: req.headers["x-verse-signature"], timestamp: req.headers["x-verse-timestamp"] });

Analytics#

analytics.scene(id, { days?, fresh? }) — GET /v1/scenes/<id>/analytics · analytics.sceneCsv(id, { days? }) — GET /v1/scenes/<id>/analytics.csv#

analytics.account({ days? }) — GET /v1/account/analytics · analytics.accountCsv({ days? }) — GET /v1/account/analytics.csv#

What Studio's Analytics page shows, for your own dashboards: views, unique and returning viewers, time spent, the funnel, devices, rooms, heatmap, daily series (days: 7, 30 — the default — or 90). The Csv variants resolve the CSV text. Owner token required.

Code
const a = await verse.analytics.scene(sceneId, { days: 7 });
console.log(`${a.views} views · ${a.uniqueViewers} people · median ${a.time.medianSeconds}s`);
const csv = await verse.analytics.accountCsv({ days: 90 });

Embed code#

embedCode(scene, { share?, poster?, background?, look?, aspect?, load?, autoplayTour?, title? })#

Pure (no request): { element, iframe, url, script } — the <verse-viewer> tag with its script, the lazy /embed iframe (what the oEmbed endpoint returns) and the URL behind it. Pass share for a private scene.

oembed(link, { maxwidth?, maxheight? }) — GET /oembed#

The oEmbed JSON a CMS fetches for a share link.

defineViewer(baseUrl)#

Loads embed.js once so <verse-viewer> is defined on the page.

Code
const { element } = verse.embedCode(sceneId, { poster: posterUrl, autoplayTour: true });
document.querySelector("#listing").innerHTML = element; // or paste it into your CMS

Scenes#

Owner-only unless noted (401 without a token, 404 for a stranger).

scenes.list() — GET /v1/account/scenes · scenes.get(id)#

Every scene the token owns, newest first; get(id) is the one entry (there is no per-scene GET route — see Warts).

Code
for (const s of await verse.scenes.list()) console.log(s.id, s.visibility, s.stats.opens);

Each entry (2.8) also says path ("fidelity" | "streamed"), glbUrl for a Fidelity scene and, for a streamed one, engine { version, current, older } — older means a newer compiler is on this server (Studio's "re-upload to get the latest look" badge).

scenes.current(id) — GET /v1/scenes/<id>/current#

Public (private scenes: owner or share token): which version the link serves and the viewer's cache key.

Code
const { version, file } = await verse.scenes.current(id); // { version: 2, file: "ingest/<id>.vpk?v=2" }

scenes.analytics(id, { days?, fresh? }) — GET /v1/scenes/<id>/analytics · scenes.analyticsCsv(id, { days? }) — GET /v1/scenes/<id>/analytics.csv#

4.0, owner-only: the Studio dashboard's numbers for one scene — views, unique and returning viewers, time, funnel, devices, rooms, viewpoints, heatmap, daily series (docs/api.md § Analytics).

Code
const a = await verse.scenes.analytics(rec.job, { days: 7 });
console.log(a.views, a.uniqueViewers, a.funnel.map((f) => `${f.label}: ${f.n}`));

scenes.claim(id) — POST /v1/scenes/<id>/claim#

Take ownership of an anonymous scene (409 if someone else owns it).

scenes.setVisibility(id, visibility) — PATCH /v1/scenes/<id>#

"public" · "unlisted" (default) · "private".

Code
await verse.scenes.setVisibility(id, "private");

scenes.shares.create(id) — POST /v1/scenes/<id>/share · scenes.shares.list(id) — GET /v1/scenes/<id>/share · scenes.shares.revoke(id, shareId) — DELETE /v1/scenes/<id>/share/<shareId>#

Per-recipient share tokens for a private scene. The token is shown once.

Code
const link = await verse.scenes.shares.create(id);
send(verse.shareLink(id, { share: link.shareToken }));
await verse.scenes.shares.revoke(id, link.id);

scenes.shares.link(id, { variant?, cfg?, view? })#

Mint a token and build the private link in one call → { id, suffix, created, shareToken, url }; revoke with scenes.shares.revoke(id, link.id).

scenes.stats(id) — GET /v1/scenes/<id>/stats#

{ opens, uniqueSessions, totalMinutes, last7d }.

scenes.heatmap(id, { fresh? }) — GET /v1/scenes/<id>/heatmap#

Where visitors stood and where they waited for bytes, as a grid over the floor plan, plus the funnel. fresh: true refolds the telemetry log.

Code
const heat = await verse.scenes.heatmap(id);
console.log(heat.funnel, heat.grid.nx, heat.grid.nz, heat.grid.stood.length);

scenes.config(id, { share? }) — GET /v1/scenes/<id>/config · scenes.setConfig(id, schema | null) — PUT /v1/scenes/<id>/config#

Configurator depth (2.7): the owner's option-group schema (variants, material aliases, visibility sets, SKU + display price — see docs/api.md § Configurator). config() is public (mirrors visibility) and resolves null when the scene has none; setConfig(id, null) clears. shareLink() takes a cfg knob for a pre-picked configuration.

Code
await verse.scenes.setConfig(id, { currency: "USD", groups: [{ id: "fabric", name: "Fabric", options: [{ id: "oak", name: "Oak", variant: "Oak" }, { id: "walnut", name: "Walnut", variant: "Walnut", price: 120 }] }] });
const rec = await verse.scenes.config(id); // { scene, config, updated } | null
verse.shareLink(id, { cfg: { fabric: "walnut" } }); // …&cfg=fabric:walnut

scenes.delete(id) — DELETE /v1/scenes/<id>#

Removes the artifact, sidecars, poster, review comments and versions; every share link stops working.

scenes.arUrl(id, { share?, version? }) — GET /ingest/<id>.usdz#

(2.7) The iOS AR Quick Look package of a product-scale scene (See it in your room) — a URL, no request. It exists only when the finished job record carries arUrl (under the AR caps, not an interior; job.ar.skipped says why otherwise). Same visibility as the scene (share for a private one), version pins a scene version. Put it in Safari's AR link shape — an <a rel="ar"> with an <img> as its first child — and iPhones open it in AR:

Code
const done = await verse.waitForJob(job);
if (done.arUrl) {
  link.rel = "ar";
  link.href = verse.scenes.arUrl(sceneId, { share: token?.shareToken });
  link.innerHTML = `<img src="${done.poster ?? "poster.png"}" alt="">View in AR`;
}

Versions#

An owned streamed (.vpk) scene takes a new upload as a version; the share link never changes (Scene versions).

versions.upload(id, file, { name? }) — POST /v1/scenes/<id>/versions (GLB body)#

Compiles the upload as an ordinary job; resolves { id, job, pending: true, url }.

versions.publish(id, file, options?)#

versions.upload() + waitForJob(), resolving the promoted record (sceneId, version, diffSummary).

Code
const v2 = await verse.versions.publish(id, readFileSync("flat-v2.glb"), { name: "flat-v2" });
console.log(`now version ${v2.version}: ${v2.diffSummary}`);

versions.attach(id, job) — POST /v1/scenes/<id>/versions (JSON { job })#

Attach a job this account uploaded through /v1/ingest.

versions.list(id) — GET /v1/scenes/<id>/versions#

Code
const { current, versions } = await verse.versions.list(id);
versions.forEach((v) => console.log(v.n, v.current ? "*" : " ", v.tris, v.diffSummary));

versions.diff(id, n) — GET /v1/scenes/<id>/versions/<n>/diff#

Version n against the version before it: triangles, clusters, size, bounds, materials added/removed/changed, texture resolution changes, summary.

versions.activate(id, n) — POST /v1/scenes/<id>/versions/<n>/activate#

Rollback or forward; the link now serves version n.

Code
await verse.versions.activate(id, 1); // roll back

versions.fileUrl(id, n) — GET /v1/scenes/<id>/versions/<n>/file · versions.stageUrl(id, n) — GET /v1/scenes/<id>/versions/<n>/stage#

Owner-only URLs of an archived version's .vpk (Range supported) and its staging manifest, for your own fetch with verse.authHeaders().

versions.delete(id, n) — DELETE /v1/scenes/<id>/versions/<n>#

Never the current one (409).

Review comments#

Pinned comments in 3D on a shared scene (Review comments). A private scene needs the owner's token or a share token (share option here, or the client's share).

review.post(scene, { pos, text, author? }, { share? }) — POST /v1/review/<sceneId>#

No account needed (60/hour/IP). pos is a world position — the embed's pick() gives you one.

Code
const hit = await viewer.pick(0.5, 0.5);
await verse.review.post(id, { pos: hit.position, text: "Oak finish here?", author: "Priya" });

review.list(scene, { share? }) — GET /v1/review/<sceneId>#

review.resolve(scene, commentId) — POST /v1/review/<sceneId>/<id>/resolve · review.delete(scene, commentId) — DELETE /v1/review/<sceneId>/<id>#

Owner moderation.

Code
for (const c of await verse.review.list(id)) if (!c.resolved) await verse.review.resolve(id, c.id);

scenes.experiences(id) — GET /v1/scenes/<id>/experiences · scenes.setDefaultExperience(id, exp) — PUT /v1/scenes/<id>/experience · scenes.defaultExperience(id) — GET /v1/scenes/<id>/experience#

Guided tours (2.7): the experiences an owner authored for a scene, which one the plain share link plays (default), and — public — that manifest.

Code
const { experiences, default: current } = await verse.scenes.experiences(id);
await verse.scenes.setDefaultExperience(id, experiences[0].id); // null clears
const rec = await verse.scenes.defaultExperience(id); // null when none is set

scenes.setGround(id, png) — PUT /v1/scenes/<id>/ground#

Exterior kit (2.7): upload the scene's ground heightfield (a PNG ≤ 4096², red = height) → { scene, path, url, width, height, bytes }. The viewer's ground.heightfield points at path.

Code
const { path } = await verse.scenes.setGround(id, await fs.promises.readFile("terrain.png"));
viewer.setExterior({ ground: { kind: "heightfield", heightfield: `/${path}`, amplitude: 8, material: "grass" } });

scenes.background(id) — GET /v1/scenes/<id>/background · scenes.setBackground(id, bg) — PUT /v1/scenes/<id>/background · scenes.setBackgroundImage(id, file, type) — PUT /v1/scenes/<id>/background/image#

Background (2.8): what sits behind the scene, one spec string (rrggbb, transparent, grad:a,b, studio:neutral|warm|dark, image:…, hdr:…; "" clears). background() is readable by whoever may open the scene (null when none is set); the setters are owner-only.

Code
await verse.scenes.setBackground(id, "grad:2a2f45,0b0d12");
await verse.scenes.setBackgroundImage(id, await fs.promises.readFile("studio.hdr"), "image/vnd.radiance");
const { bg } = (await verse.scenes.background(id)) ?? {};

scenes.media(id) — GET /v1/scenes/<id>/media · scenes.setMedia(id, table) — PUT /v1/scenes/<id>/media · scenes.uploadMedia(id, file) — POST /v1/scenes/<id>/media/upload#

Media surfaces + spatial audio (2.7): videos on surfaces and ambient sounds, stored with the scene. media() is public (mirrors the scene's visibility; null when none), the other two owner-only. uploadMedia takes one raw file (mp4 / webm video ≤ 200 MB, mp3 / m4a / ogg / wav / webm audio ≤ 20 MB, sniffed) and answers { path, url, bytes, kind, ext }; put the path in a surface's or emitter's url (same-origin only).

Code
const clip = await verse.scenes.uploadMedia(id, fs.readFileSync("tv-loop.mp4"), "video/mp4");
const bed = await verse.scenes.uploadMedia(id, fs.readFileSync("lobby.mp3"), "audio/mpeg");
await verse.scenes.setMedia(id, {
  media: [{ material: 3, url: `/${clip.path}`, emissive: 1.5, audio: true }],
  audio: [{ pos: [2, 1.2, -1], url: `/${bed.path}`, radius: 6, gain: 0.8 }],
});
const table = await verse.scenes.media(id); // { scene, media, audio } | null

Publishing#

publishExperience(manifest) — POST /v1/experience#

A .verse.json manifest → { path, url }.

Code
const { url } = await verse.publishExperience({ name: "Showroom", scene: `ingest/${id}.vpk`,
  hotspots: [{ id: "front", label: "Front", position: [0, 1.2, 3], look: [0, 0.5, 0] }] });

experience.get(id) — GET /v1/experience/<id> · experience.update(id, manifest) — PUT /v1/experience/<id> · experience.uploadMedia(id, clip, contentType?) — POST /v1/experience/<id>/media#

A version-2 manifest (ExperienceManifest: hotspots with anchor pins and cards, tour.steps with poses + narration, sun) read fresh (no-store), rewritten in place (owner-only), and narration clips (≤ 2 MB, mp3/m4a/ogg/ wav/webm) whose path a step's audio references.

Code
const { experience } = await verse.experience.get("exp-38fd878a72");
const clip = await verse.experience.uploadMedia("exp-38fd878a72", mp3Bytes, "audio/mpeg");
experience.tour.steps[0].audio = `/${clip.path}`;
await verse.experience.update("exp-38fd878a72", experience);

publishTour(tour) — POST /v1/tour#

{ name?, scene, samples: [[t, x, y, z, fx, fy, fz], …] } → a ?tour= link.

uploadPoster(png, { scene? }) — POST /v1/poster#

Raw PNG ≤ 4 MB; with a token and scene, attached as that scene's thumbnail.

Presence rooms#

rooms.eventsUrl(room) — GET /v1/room/<room>/events · rooms.pose(room, pose) — POST /v1/room/<room>/pose · rooms.signal(room, msg) — POST /v1/room/<room>/signal#

Code
const es = new EventSource(verse.rooms.eventsUrl("demo-room") + "?id=viewer-1"); // ?id= tags the stream (2.7)
es.onmessage = (e) => console.log(JSON.parse(e.data).peers);
es.addEventListener("signal", (e) => console.log("signal", JSON.parse(e.data)));
setInterval(() => verse.rooms.pose("demo-room", { id: "viewer-1", name: "Me", color: "#78aaff", pose: cam, flags: { hand: true } }), 125);
await verse.rooms.signal("demo-room", { from: "viewer-1", to: "*", kind: "present", data: { on: true } });

rooms.signal is the relay the viewer's voice (WebRTC offers / answers / ICE) and presenter mode (present, action, hand, handover) use; the server forwards it and stores nothing. Kinds and the action schema: api.md § Presence rooms.

Signing and operations#

pubkey() — GET /v1/pubkey · config() — GET /v1/config · health() — GET /v1/health/deep · ingestStats() — GET /v1/ops/ingest-stats#

Code
const { spki } = await verse.pubkey();             // Ed25519 SPKI, base64
const h = await verse.health().catch((e) => e.body); // 503 → VerseError; its body still carries `checks`
const { last24h } = await verse.ingestStats();      // any account

sendTelemetry(batch) — POST /v1/telemetry#

One batch → 204. Returns false without a request when the client opted out.

Low level#

request(path, { method?, body?, headers?, query?, signal?, retries?, parse? })#

Any route with the SDK's auth, error contract and retry. Plain objects are sent as JSON; bytes as-is; parse: "response" returns the raw Response.

Code
const leads = await verse.request("/v1/ops/leads"); // operator-only; needs the admin token
const vpk = await verse.request(`/v1/scenes/${id}/versions/2/file`, { parse: "response", headers: { Range: "bytes=0-1023" } });

url(path, query?) · authHeaders()#

The absolute URL for a path, and the headers to use with your own fetch.

Embed#

embedViewer(target, options) · verse.embed(target, options)#

Loads embed.js from the Verse origin once and mounts the engine in an iframe from that origin (your page needs no COOP/COEP headers). Resolves the VerseViewer — every verb and event of the embed SDK, fully typed. Options: every VerseEmbedOptions (scene, vpk, model, poster, variant, lights, cinematic, share, review, analytics, quality, render, hdr, bg) plus baseUrl (the Verse origin; verse.embed() fills it in), scriptUrl, waitForReady, timeoutMs. 2.7 adds the light studio (viewer.setLights({...}), lights event, VerseLightsState) and Cinematic stills (viewer.setCinematic(true), cinematic event, viewer.saveStill({ preset: "1080p" }) → VerseStillResult) — see embed-sdk.md. 2.7.2 adds Auto look (viewer.autoLook() → VerseAutoLookResult, auto-look events, undoAutoLook()): one call for the best view, exposure, sun, fill, shadows, sky, the quality knobs and the walkthrough — see embed-sdk.md.

Code
import { embedViewer } from "https://HOST/sdk/verse-sdk.js";
const viewer = await embedViewer(document.getElementById("stage"), { baseUrl: "https://HOST", scene: SCENE_ID, variant: "Oak" });
viewer.on("variant", ({ names }) => renderPicker(names));   // KHR_materials_variants in the scene
picker.onchange = () => viewer.setVariant(picker.value);     // or null for the file's defaults
viewer.on("loaded", (d) => console.log(d.clusters, "clusters"));
viewer.setClipPlanes([[0, -1, 0, 1.2]]);                    // 2.7: section cut (keep y ≤ 1.2)
viewer.measure("distance");                                 // 2.7: taps → `measure` events

A complete page with a variant picker: sdk/examples/embed-variants.html, served live at https://HOST/sdk/embed-variants.html?scene=<id>.

Telemetry opt-out#

The SDK sends exactly one kind of row on its own: an upload-fail beacon to POST /v1/telemetry when an upload fails client-side or a job ends in error — the same row the web app sends, so the operator's 24 h scan counts failures the server never logged. It carries the error text, the phase and the taxonomy code; never the file, the token or an IP.

Code
new VerseClient({ baseUrl, telemetry: false }); // the SDK never calls /v1/telemetry on its own

The viewer's own analytics (the look-and-stall feed behind the heatmap) are a separate opt-out: embedViewer(el, { analytics: false }), exactly like the embed option.

Examples#

FileWhat
sdk/examples/upload-and-link.mjsNode CLI: node upload-and-link.mjs scene.glb --server https://HOST [--token …] [--name …] [--private] — prints the share link (and a share token for a private scene)
sdk/examples/embed-variants.htmlplain HTML: SDK from /sdk/verse-sdk.js, viewer + a material-variant picker built from the variant event (served at /sdk/embed-variants.html)
sdk/examples/publish.ymlGitHub Actions: publish assets/*.glb on every push to main, write the links to the job summary

Tests and gates#

  • cd sdk && npm test — unit tests (node:test) against a scripted mock origin: headers, error contract, retry rules, resumable parts/resync/409, cancel, progress, every route's method + path, telemetry opt-out.
  • npm run test:integration — the SDK against a real serve.mjs (ports 8750–8759): upload → poll → done → link → own → share → review → heatmap → version → diff → activate → delete.
  • node web/test/fix-verify-sdk.mjs — both of the above, plus: the build is current (served copy and embed typings in sync), /sdk/verse-sdk.js is served with embed.js's headers and loads in a browser, the Postman collection is byte-identical to scripts/gen-postman.mjs's output, and scripts/api-parity.mjs reports zero drift between the server's dispatch, docs/api.md, this page and the SDK.

Warts#

API shapes the SDK papers over rather than changes:

  • No per-scene GET. scenes.get(id) filters GET /v1/account/scenes; a single-scene read for a non-owner does not exist (use scenes.current for the version facts).
  • Promotion lags done. A new version's job answers status: "done" a beat before it is archived and diffed; versions.publish() keeps polling until version is on the record.
  • One-shot upload progress is only available in browsers (XHR); Node's fetch has no upload progress — use the resumable flow for a bar.
  • .d.ts MIME. The server has no MIME entry for .ts, so /sdk/verse-sdk.d.ts (like /verse-embed.d.ts) is served as application/octet-stream; editors fetching it directly see a download.
  • No CORS on /v1/*. Browser pages on a foreign origin cannot call the API; only the presence SSE stream, /ingest/* artifacts, /oembed and the three third-party scripts (embed.js, /sdk/verse-viewer.js, /sdk/verse-sdk.js) carry Access-Control-Allow-Origin. Use the package server-side, or host the page on the Verse origin. The embed path is unaffected.
